sentences.text: Hypselospinus was a lightly built iguanodontian estimated to be 6 meters long.
Richard Lydekker first described the dinosaur in 1889 as a species of Iguanodon, but David Norman reclassified the fossils into the separate genus Hypselospinus in May 2010.

The specific name 'fittoni' honors William Henry Fitton, who worked in Early Cretaceous strata in England, where remains were discovered in the Lower Cretaceous Wadhurst Clay of Shornden, East Sussex.
The type specimen was found in Shornden Quarry, located over a distance of 50 yards.
Hypselospinus belongs to the parent group Neoiguanodontia and is classified within the class Ornithischia.

Hypselospinus lived during the lower Valanginian stage, approximately 140 million years ago, though its time range spans from the Berriasian to the Valanginian, between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago.

It is debated whether I. hollingtoniensis should be included within I. fittoni, with some researchers retaining it as a separate species. A group of scientists independently reclassified I. fittoni into the genus Wadhurstia, making it a junior synonym of Hypselospinus.
